solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This writer's put out about lively frolic, unrehearsed

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: 'this writer is' gives I'M

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of put go about, that is around, the frolic
'put out' tells us the word put is knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: a romp is a lively frolic

explanation.surface: A writer is annoyed by some boisterous fun that nobody planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as 'annoyed', but it is an instruction: rearrange put to PTU, which 'about' then wraps round the frolic to make PROMPTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, with no preparation or rehearsal.

clue.text: Amateur in grip of old pro, substantial?

indicators.note: held in the grip of means placed inside the other word

parts.note: moll is an archaic word for a prostitute, a 'pro'

explanation.surface: An amateur caught in the clutches of a veteran professional asks whether he is substantial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in grip of' puts A inside MOLL. The definition is playful: molal relates to the mole, the chemist's unit of amount of substance, hence 'substantial?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Molal concentration is measured in moles of solute, so the word concerns quantity of substance in a chemistry sense.

clue.text: Dad's enveloped by homily as of old, gassy stuff

indicators.note: wrapped up inside the other word

parts.note: prone is an obsolete word for a homily or sermon
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Father is smothered by an old-fashioned sermon full of hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enveloped by' signals insertion; the homily word is an archaism found in Chambers, which Azed solvers are expected to consult.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a hydrocarbon gas used as fuel, so it is literally gaseous material.

clue.text: Naiad involving us in a lark, swimming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming move about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A water nymph joins us for some fun in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: US is put in A LARK and 'swimming' rearranges the whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusalka is a Slavic water spirit, a kind of river nymph like the Greek naiads.

clue.text: Ribs? Huge, emerging from college shortly

indicators.note: emerging out of the shell, so the outer letters are shed and the middle remains
from says the short form of college comes away from the big word, its first three letters at the front

parts.note: colossal means huge
COLL is the short form of college; its COL comes off the front and its final L off the end

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an enormous serving of ribs on leaving college.
explanation.walkthrough: The short form of college is split round the answer: 'from' strips its front three letters, leaving OSSAL, and 'emerging' sheds the last, like a chick leaving its shell. OS (outsize) for 'huge' is a tempting false start.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural for bones, and ribs are examples of bones, hence the question mark.

clue.text: With HM no longer on board, bales ship out? We'll go off rapidly

indicators.note: on board means taken inside the other letters
the letters of bales and ship are put out of order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Her Majesty but reigns no longer

explanation.surface: With the late Queen gone from the ship, its cargo of bales is unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the bales and ship to PISHABLES, and 'on board' slips the royal cipher inside; 'no longer' because Elizabeth II has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishable goods spoil quickly, so they are food items that decay fast.

clue.text: Old decoy, name separate, inverted

indicators.note: turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the letters backwards

parts.note: apart means separate

explanation.surface: An old decoy's name is separate and upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapan, an old variant of trepan, was someone who lured others into a trap, a decoy.

clue.text: Roman magistrate? See special one in seat

indicators.note: the answer is the one that sits in the seat after special, so it is what remains

parts.note: a sedile is a seat for officiating clergy in a church

explanation.surface: A Roman official is told to look at a particular person in a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDILE is S plus the answer: 'one in' seat after S (special) is what is left when S goes. 'See' just tells the solver to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Edile is a variant spelling of aedile, a magistrate of ancient Rome in charge of public works.

clue.text: Contract top to bottom in frame

indicators.note: in a down answer the first letter is moved from the top to the bottom

parts.note: a lease is a contract to rent property

explanation.surface: An instruction to tighten something from top to bottom within a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun LEASE, and 'top to bottom' moves its L to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden stand or framework that holds a painting.

clue.text: Bile after rest's disturbed — I'll sever friendship

indicators.note: anger is placed after the rearranged letters
the word rest is disturbed, its letters shaken up

parts.note: bile is used figuratively to mean anger

explanation.surface: Bad temper after a broken night leads someone to end a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: An estranger is one who estranges, alienating friends and ending a close relationship.

clue.text: Cluster of cells, type wherein time's passed, American

indicators.note: time has passed, meaning it has gone from the word

parts.note: sort means type or kind

explanation.surface: An American describes a type of cell cluster that has had its day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorus is a cluster of spore cases on the underside of a fern frond.

clue.text: Study beyond traditional methods rate limiting compound of arsenic

indicators.note: the outer word limits, or encloses, the other letters

parts.note: pace means rate of progress

indicators.note: a compound is a new combination, so the letters of arsenic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lab study of how fast arsenic compounds react, done outside the usual methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound of' fits the chemistry surface but asks for arsenic rearranged, to RASCIEN, which 'limiting' has the rate word enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Parascience deals with phenomena, such as telepathy, that lie outside the scope of conventional scientific inquiry.

clue.text: Coarse Scots ground-bass regularly missed out

indicators.note: every other letter is missed out, starting with the first

parts.note: the letters taken as written; the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th survive

explanation.surface: A rough Scottish musician regularly leaves out the ground bass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missed out' drops G, O, N, B and S from GROUND-BASS. A ground bass is a repeated bass line in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudas is a Scots adjective for rough, coarse or uncouth, as in a rudas old woman.

clue.text: Fine wastage?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
loss means wastage

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue also defines the answer: the fine threads wasted from a silk cocoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Floss is the rough silk round a cocoon, a fine waste product of silk-making.

clue.text: Student of e.g. Saudi culture, one twice engrossed in pictures etc

indicators.note: absorbed in, so placed inside the other word

parts.note: art covers pictures and the like
A means one, as in a single thing
bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: A scholar of Saudi life gets very absorbed in paintings and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one twice' suggests two I's, but it is A plus BIS, which is 'engrossed in' ART.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a scholar of Arabic language and Arab civilization, of which Saudi Arabia is part.

clue.text: Rodent fancying sweet bulbs in quantity — once worth trapping it

indicators.note: the old word for worth traps the quantity inside it

parts.note: carat once meant worth or value, an obsolete sense
mass is a quantity of matter

explanation.surface: A rodent with a taste for sweet bulbs, eaten in quantity, was once worth catching.
explanation.definitionFit: The camass rat is a North American pocket gopher that feeds on the edible bulbs of the camass plant.

clue.text: One extracting hemp seeds, Jack maybe, bagging pound

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, putting inside

parts.note: Jack the Ripper is the notorious Victorian murderer
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A notorious Jack grabs a pound while stripping seeds from hemp.
explanation.definitionFit: A rippler uses a toothed tool, a ripple, to strip the seeds from flax or hemp.

clue.text: All confused maid admits being rendered speechless

indicators.note: lets in, so the mixed letters go inside

parts.note: aia, or ayah, is an Indian word for a nursemaid or maid

indicators.note: the letters of all are confused, mixed up

explanation.surface: A maid, completely flustered, admits to being left lost for words.
explanation.definitionFit: Alalia is the medical term for loss or absence of the power of speech.

clue.text: Fair component of some resins, not mine

indicators.note: not mine means the letters of mine are removed

parts.note: melamine is used to make synthetic resins

explanation.surface: A fair resin ingredient, but not one I own.
explanation.definitionFit: A mela is a Hindu festival or fair in South Asia.

clue.text: Ikon crafted with silence by number in shared meal? It's typical of cloistered community

indicators.note: in says the rearranged icon, the hush and the number all go inside the meal

parts.note: a mess is a meal eaten together, as in the armed forces

indicators.note: crafted means skilfully reshaped, so the letters of Ikon are rearranged

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: An icon is made in silence by a member of a monastery at a communal meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkishness is the quality or manner of monks, who live as a cloistered religious community.

clue.text: Fruity cluster eater demolished with joyous cry

indicators.note: demolished means broken up, so the letters of eater are rearranged

parts.note: io is a classical cry of joy or triumph

explanation.surface: Someone devours a bunch of fruit and whoops with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' plays on its sense of eating something up, and turns EATER into ETAER.
explanation.definitionFit: An etaerio is a botanical term for an aggregate fruit such as a raspberry, a cluster of small fruitlets.

clue.text: Chant involving consecutive trio like wind among the leaves?

indicators.note: taking in, so wrapping round

parts.note: to sing is to chant
GHI are three consecutive letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A chant performed by three singers sounds like a breeze through trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The wind is said to sigh in the trees, making a soft murmuring sound like a person's sigh.

clue.text: Work in bank, say, gets captain confused

indicators.note: the letters of gets and captain are confused, mixed up

explanation.surface: A banking job leaves the captain bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' mixes GETS and CAPTAIN together. The bank is a peat bank, not a financial one.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat-casting is the job of cutting turves of peat from a peat bank, which is an earthy bank, not a financial one.

clue.text: Fashionable number turned up in this cut?

indicators.note: in says the upturned number sits inside the rearranged word
cut means chopped about, so the letters of this are rearranged
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A number turns up in this fashionable cut, as at a hairdresser's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down entry, reading upwards to ON; 'cut' usually loses a last letter, but here shuffles this to TISH, and 'in' puts ON inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonish means stylish or modish, from ton, high fashion or society.

clue.text: A wee bittie whiskey imbibed by soak?

indicators.note: drunk in, so placed inside

parts.note: a sop is something soaked, as bread dipped in liquid
W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Just a small drop of whisky, taken by a heavy drinker?
explanation.walkthrough: A soak is a drunkard in the surface; here it means SOP, and 'imbibed by' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowp is a Scots word meaning a small quantity, a sup, matching the Scots 'wee bittie'.

clue.text: Duck portion? It may deceive the eye (5, two words)

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a part is a portion

explanation.surface: A cut of duck might fool the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is abstract art using patterns that create optical illusions of movement.

clue.text: Drunk, having imbibed gallon, sky high?

indicators.note: having drunk in, so containing

parts.note: winy can mean intoxicated with wine

explanation.surface: A drunk who has downed a gallon is flying high.
explanation.definitionFit: Wingy means having wings or soaring, so something up in the sky, with a hint of being 'high'.

clue.text: An old field having parts switched for hunt?

indicators.note: the front part and the end part trade places

parts.note: an gives A
glebe is an old word for a field or land, especially a parish's land

explanation.surface: A historic field is reorganised for hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having parts switched' splits A GLEBE into AGLE and BE and swaps them.
explanation.definitionFit: To beagle is to go hunting hares with beagles, the small hounds bred for it.

clue.text: Subject I sat in e.g. poly, missing pass at first

indicators.note: I sat inside the remaining letters
the pass is missing, removed from the word
the removal is at the start of the word

parts.note: a poly, or polytechnic, is an example of a college
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A student sat in a lecture at a polytechnic but failed the first exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests an exam but is a mountain pass; 'missing' and 'at first' drop it from the front, leaving LEGE, and 'sat in' seats I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a vassal owing feudal service, so a subject of a lord or monarch.

clue.text: Mountain plant, strangely pleasing, one picked out

indicators.note: strangely means oddly arranged, so the letters are mixed up
the letter for one is picked out of the mix and discarded

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: A mountain plant, oddly attractive, is singled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel is baldmoney, an umbelliferous herb of mountain pastures.

clue.text: Painful swelling making one miss work in career

indicators.note: to miss the work means it is omitted

parts.note: to career is to rush along, like a gallop
OP is the abbreviation for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A sore swelling makes someone miss work and harms their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is a noun in the surface but a verb meaning to rush, GALLOP; 'miss' drops OP from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gall is a sore on the skin caused by rubbing, a painful swelling, especially on a horse.

clue.text: Scots engineer, no longer vigorous in energy

parts.note: rank once meant vigorous or strong; 'no longer' marks the sense as archaic
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Scottish engineer has lost his energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer vigorous' looks like a description of weakness but marks an archaic sense of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rankine was a Scottish engineer and physicist, after whom the Rankine temperature scale and cycle are named.

clue.text: One born in spring period, English, with rain swirling around

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
the letters of rain swirl about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone born in spring in England with rain swirling round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arien is a person born under Aries, the zodiac sign covering late March to April, in spring.

clue.text: Butterfly? It's thrown out in air gusts

indicators.note: the letters of it's are thrown out, discarded from the phrase
in says the letters to discard are found within the phrase air gusts, spread through it

explanation.surface: A butterfly is tossed about in gusty winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's thrown out in' removes the letters of It's from AIR GUSTS: the I goes from AIR, leaving ARGUSTS, then the TS from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The argus is a type of butterfly with eye-like spots on its wings, after the many-eyed Argus of myth.

clue.text: Heather may be so wrinkled around onset of greying

indicators.note: the wrinkled word goes around the letter

parts.note: liny means marked with lines, wrinkled

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: G is the first letter of greying

explanation.surface: Heather, perhaps a woman, is wrinkled and starting to go grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' greying gives G, and 'around' has LINY wrap it. Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, and ling is heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingy means covered in ling, which is heather, so a heathery moor is lingy.

clue.text: Student of religious stuff hereto revised, taking in record of work done

indicators.note: taking in means including inside
revised means reworked, so the letters of hereto are rearranged

parts.note: a log is a written record, as of work carried out

explanation.surface: A religious scholar has rewritten old material and added a work diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologer is an old word for a theologian, a scholar of divinity.
